title: Three improved lower bounds for hypergraph Ramsey numbers: R(4,4,4;3) >= 84, R(4,6;3) >= 64, R(5,5;4) >= 36
description:
At a glance

cellDS1 rev #18this workwitness
R(4,4,4;3)≥ 79≥ 8483 points, 3 colours
R(4,6;3)≥ 63≥ 6463 points, 2 colours
R(5,5;4)≥ 35≥ 3635 points, 2 colours

Under DS1's convention (p.5) that R is the least n forcing a monochromatic clique, a good colouring on n points proves R ≥ n+1.

The objects, not the search

Each result is a group-invariant colouring given as a small table over group orbits rather than as solver output. For R(4,4,4;3): let p = 83, a = 9 generating the order-41 subgroup of Z_83*, and G = {x -> a^i x + b} of order 3403. G acts on the 91,881 triples of Z_83 with exactly 27 orbits, each free of size 3403; 27 numbers give the colours, nine per colour, so the three colour classes are exactly equal at 30,627. That equality is not forced: regularity only forces each class to be a multiple of 3403, and enumerating all invariant good colourings of this class gives 36 of them — twelve splitting 9/9/9 and twenty-four splitting 8/9/10. The other two use 120 and 107 orbits respectively, under group actions that are not free. Each construction regenerates its entire colouring from its table alone, with no solver, and is tested to reproduce the committed witness entry by entry.

Verification

Every one of the twelve deposited witnesses is checked by complete enumeration, each under its own hash-bound run kept in logs/. For the three headline objects that is 1,837,620 four-subsets at n = 83, 324,632 five-subsets at n = 35, and all 4- and 6-subsets of a 63-set; the other nine are scanned over their own point sets (the n = 79 witness, for instance, over 1,502,501 four-subsets). The checking is done by a verifier with a different implementation from the search code. Two distinct claims should not be run together: shares no search implementation holds for every witness, while uses no itertools holds for verify_scratch.py, which builds the face order and clique scan from explicit nested loops and is applied to the four-uniform witness; the other checkers use itertools.combinations for face indexing, which is precisely why a from-scratch third verifier exists. Under the intended convention, colour 0 contains no monochromatic K_4^(3) and colour 1 contains no monochromatic K_6^(3). A separate reversed-K_4 control counts 102,627 monochromatic K_4^(3) in colour 1. This is a discriminating control against certain implementation failures; it does not establish the colour convention or validate the K_6 branch. A separate six-vertex control assigns colour 1 to all twenty triples and requires the K_6 detector to report one violation. Negative results carry certificates too: a separate RUP/RAT proof checker re-certifies five UNSAT symmetry classes of the n = 63 tower — five of the 22 classes that pass the variable filter used, and the proof clauses themselves are not deposited — and its discriminating test weakens a real instance until it becomes satisfiable and requires the checker to refuse it.

An obstruction theorem

If an affine group satisfies |G| = C(p,2) and its multiplier subgroup has index two and omits -1 (equivalently, within that index-two family, p ≡ 3 mod 4), it acts regularly on unordered pairs, so adjoining a fixed point forces every triple through that point into a single orbit and hence one colour; no base triple may then take that colour, and, for the diagonal problem R(4,...,4;3) in m colours, the base must be coloured with m-1 colours while avoiding a monochromatic K_4^(3) — impossible only once the base reaches or exceeds the (m-1)-colour Ramsey number. At m = 3 that threshold is R(4,4;3) = 13 and both towers clear it; at m = 4 it is R(4,4,4;3) itself and p = 79 does not, so adjoining a fourth colour to the deposited 79-point witness gives a good invariant colouring of the extension. The threshold is a hypothesis, not a detail. This explains without computation why the pair-regular class of each tower here is the index-two multiplier subgroup — Z_83 : C_41, Z_79 : C_39, in neither case the top of the tower — and each of those base classes HOLDS a witness (at n = 83 and n = 79 respectively). What the theorem explains without computation is that adjoining a fixed point empties them: Z_83 : C_41 + 1 fixed and Z_79 : C_39 + 1 fixed are UNSAT. The argument needs the base to be uncolourable in one fewer colour, which holds at three colours for these primes and not in general. The order condition alone is insufficient: for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) the element -1 is a quadratic residue, every pair acquires a stabiliser, and there are two pair-orbits rather than one. The corresponding fixed-point classes are satisfiable at p = 13 and p = 37; these examples target the omitted--1 hypothesis and do not by themselves establish independence of every condition in a broader generalisation.

What is not claimed

Novelty is provisional. Both incumbents are personal communications (2018 and 2021), which were not obtained through the bibliographic sources searched; that is a search boundary rather than a claim that they can never be obtained. MathSciNet, zbMATH, Google Scholar, DataCite and the incumbent's own public addendum were searched and nothing stronger was found — the incumbent's one published paper on this topic carries zero citations in MathSciNet and one in Google Scholar, and that citing work is principally on graph Ramsey numbers, its one 3-uniform object being K_4 minus a hyperedge rather than the complete K_4^(3) of these cells — but a newer unpublished communication was not excluded by the searches reported here. No upper bound is established here: DS1 revision 18 does not display a two-sided interval for these cells. They improve the displayed lower bounds but do not close a bracket. The incumbent constructions were not re-verified here. For the two [Dyb3] cells, public-addendum files were inspected for their sizes, hashes and declared vertex counts, but were not re-verified as colourings. The [Ex24] construction underlying the DS1 entry for R(5,5;4) was not obtained through the documented retrieval channels. The comparison for that cell is therefore with the bound recorded in DS1, not with an independently inspected incumbent witness. Every negative result is a statement about a symmetry class, never about a Ramsey number — a class can be empty while the cell is wide open. And Runtime is not a novelty argument. A short local run can coexist with prior unpublished, poorly indexed or differently described work; the priority limits above remain in force.
